World Cup 2026 Group I preview: Prediction, odds, full team overviews - Yahoo Sports
[...]
Group I might be the closest thing this World Cup has to a Group of Death with three teams — France, Senegal and Norway— that look capable of making a run. Iraq is in the unfortunate position of having to play all three of them.
[...]
Teams listed in predicted order of finish. * indicates third-place team predicted to advance to the knockout stage.
[...]
Odds: +750

What you need to know: The Lions of Téranga won their second Africa Cup of Nations title on the field in January, but lost it later after a ruling by Africa’s confederation that Senegal had forfeited by walking off the field in protest of a penalty being awarded to Morocco. Regardless, Senegal has all the makings of a rising power going into this World Cup, with the trio of Sadio Mané, Nicolas Jackson and Iliman Ndiaye providing some attacking punch ahead of world-class center back and captain Kalidou Koulibaly and keeper Edouard Mendy.
[...]
How they play: Senegal has a fluid attack and a front three that can float between different positions to cause confusion in defense. Ismaïla Sarr looks like the best option to play behind them, while players such as Pape Matar Sarr, Pape Gueye and Idrissa Gueye can fit into more defensive roles. Coach Pape Thiaw can set his team up in a 4-3-3 or a 4-2-3-1.
[...]
Star player: Mané has been out of the spotlight since moving from Bayern Munich to Saudi Arabia in 2023, and at 34 years old, he’s not the same player who set the Premier League on fire with Liverpool. But he still has the gravitas and ability of a superstar, enters the tournament as Senegal’s all-time leading goal-scorer and can take over a game on his day.
[...]
World Cup history: A 2002 quarterfinal appearance is Senegal’s best result in four appearances at the competition, all of which came this century. A 3-0 Round of 16 defeat to England ended its campaign in Qatar, but bettering that finish is an achievable goal for Senegal as it comes stateside.

Senegal head into the 2026 World Cup with confidence and pedigree, having topped their CAF qualifying group ahead of DR Congo and Mauritania. Under head coach Pape Thiaw, the Lions of Teranga look powerful and experienced, a side capable of springing a surprise at odds of 125‑1.

Ranked 14th by FIFA, The Lions of Teranga are again built around the spine of Sadio Mané, Kalidou Koulibaly, and Édouard Mendy, with Idrissa Gana Gueye and Iliman Ndiaye, who add balance and creativity. Gueye’s defensive discipline and Ndiaye’s flair between the lines give Senegal a strong core. Add to that their wide threats and physicality which make them dangerous in transition. They open against France in New Jersey. That’s a fixture that evokes memories of their famous 1‑0 win over Les Bleus in 2002, before facing Norway and Iraq. Yet with the expanded format allowing third‑place teams to progress, Senegal can afford to be pragmatic early and target Iraq in their final match.

A 3‑1 win over England at Nottingham Forest’s City Ground last summer underlined their quality. Thiaw’s preferred 4‑3‑3 or 4‑2‑3‑1 system maximises their athleticism and organisation, and with form, experience, and belief on their side, Senegal look ready to push beyond the group stage and perhaps claim another major scalp along the way.

results.title: Senegal World Cup Odds: Predictions and Value Bets for 2026
highlights:
Senegal arrive at the 2026 World Cup carrying genuine knockout-round credentials, an unbeaten qualifying record, and a squad stacked with European top-flight talent. The outright market ranks them 20th of 48 teams, with the best available price sitting at +10000 at BetOnline and Lucky Rebel, reflecting both the quality in their group and the reality that, on paper, they are contenders to go deep rather than to lift the trophy. The more interesting conversation is not whether they win it all, but which market best captures the value in a team that has reached the Round of 16 at back-to-back World Cups and enters 2026 with unfinished business.
[...]
- Best Pick: Senegal To Reach the Round of 16
- Confidence: 3.5 / 5
- Best Odds: +10000 (Outright Winner, BetOnline / Lucky Rebel)
- Reason: A tough Group I draw versus France and Norway caps the outright ceiling, but Senegal’s defensive solidity and attacking depth make knockout-round progression the defensible market angle.
[...]
Group I is the most difficult assignment Senegal could have drawn. France are among the tournament favourites, and Norway, powered by Erling Haaland, represent a genuine threat for second place. The Iraq fixture on June 26 in Toronto is the game Senegal will target for maximum points, but navigating past both France and Norway to top the group looks an uphill task. A more realistic scenario sees them finish second or third and enter the expanded Round of 32 bracket.
[...]
The Quarter-Finals represent the ceiling of realistic expectation given the bracket and the squad’s age profile. The betting structure that reflects this most accurately is not the outright at +10000, where Senegal need to beat five or six elite opponents consecutively, but a stage-of-elimination market centered on reaching the last 16 or last eight. That is where the value in the Senegal World Cup 2026 odds conversation sits.
[...]
Main Pick: Senegal To Reach the Round of 16 (best available price at leading operators). Senegal’s qualifying record of five wins and one draw from six games, with 16 goals scored and just two conceded, confirms a team that does not gift opponents cheap results. In the 48-team format, finishing third in Group I still offers a path through, and Iraq on June 26 is a winnable match that provides a floor of at least one group win. The defensive spine of Koulibaly, Mendy, and Gueye is World Cup-tested, and that experience matters in tight knockout moments.
[...]
The outright at +10000 is a speculative flutter at best. The stage-of-elimination market and targeted player props are the cleaner angles for Senegal World Cup 2026 tips.
